claims.text: Full DFT thermodynamic integration is prohibitively expensive because of the required phase-space sampling.
Standard EAM or similar classical potentials fail to capture complex liquid structure in multicomponent alloys.
An MLP using Holder means and local coordination descriptors can accurately predict BCC–Laves free-energy differences in Ta-based refractory HEAs.
Including high-temperature liquid-like configurations in the training set enables the MLP to capture complex multicomponent liquid structure.
Training on liquid-like configurations avoids kinetic-trapping artifacts observed with classical potentials.
Local coordination and atomic-size-induced lattice distortion drive Laves-phase formation or phase separation in refractory HEAs.
Laves-phase precipitation can reduce atomic-radius misfit and lower the elastic energy of a refractory BCC solid solution.
Holder means of group number, atomic radius, and electronegativity allow an MLP to represent local energy landscapes more accurately than EAM.
An MLP-based perturbation scheme can resolve subtle BCC–Laves free-energy differences without the cost of full DFT integration.
Strong Cr–Ta binding and a negative Cr–Ta mixing enthalpy promote Cr2Ta Laves-phase precipitation and reduce BCC stability.
Specific Cr–Ta or Cr–Nb binary interactions can drive phase separation in refractory BCC HEAs.
The predicted BCC–Laves free-energy difference will agree with experimental phase-stability trends within 5%.
The MLP perturbation scheme will reduce computational cost by more than 90% relative to full DFT thermodynamic integration.
The proposed scheme will correctly predict the onset of phase separation caused by negative mixing enthalpy rather than incorrectly stabilizing BCC through configurational entropy alone.
Kinetic effects can obscure the equilibrium free-energy landscape and produce time-dependent phase separation in high-entropy nanoalloys.
An MLP trained with liquid configurations may still fail to capture anharmonic vibrational free energy near melting.
Magnetic entropy can be significant near melting and can invalidate the proposed treatment in magnetically dominated alloys such as CoCrFeMnNi.
Local structural descriptors may fail when liquid structure is dominated by long-range ordering.
Laves precipitation is experimentally known to occur at 1200–1400 K in the proposed TaNbHfZr example system.
Phase-fraction evolution over simulation time can distinguish a thermodynamic driving force from kinetic trapping.

contradictions.description: The concrete example and proposed test use TaNbHfZr, which contains neither Cr nor Nb–Cr pairs, while the asserted decomposition mechanism and falsification rule rely principally on Cr–Ta or Cr–Nb interactions and Cr-driven Laves precipitation.
